title: 30-second romantic-fantasy drama structured-cue application
purpose: Same three baseline scenarios, rerun after adding an example consequential-moving-shot cue timeline to the existing shot template. Verbatim stateless model outputs; assessment saved separately.

method.engine: eval completion(default), three independent stateless calls

scenario_prompts.romance_approach_stop_eye_contact_reacti: Plan a 30-second AI romantic-fantasy drama: two adult characters approach each other through a moonlit enchanted garden, one stops, they make eye contact, then each reacts. Output a shot-by-shot planning table with seconds, actor blocking, camera movement, action phases, holds/reactions, continuity and AI prompts/handoff. Make it usable for production, but do not assume a reference video.
scenario_prompts.offscreen_entrance_reveal: Plan a 30-second AI romantic-fantasy drama in which one adult character is already in a moonlit hall and a second character enters from offscreen; build a reveal and reaction. Output a shot-by-shot table with seconds, actor blocking, camera movement, action phases, holds/reactions, cut continuity and AI prompt handoff. Be explicit about what is observed versus designed; no reference provided.
scenario_prompts.walk_to_dialogue_interaction: Plan a 30-second AI romantic-fantasy drama: two adult characters walk together through a moonlit garden, transition into a short dialogue interaction, and finish on a reaction. Output shot-by-shot seconds, blocking, camera movement, gait/contact visibility, action phases/cut continuity, holds/reactions and AI prompt handoff. No reference video supplied.

method.scope: No archive conclusions; no source reference footage, named generator, storyboard images, or rendered clips.

## 30-second romantic-fantasy drama — production proposal

**Status:** DESIGN_PROPOSAL; no reference video or production assets were supplied. The timings below are proposed shot-local seconds, not observed footage or universal movement timing. Character, location, model, and camera-control support remain unconfirmed. **Both characters are adults.**

| Shot / final time | Actor blocking & action phases | Camera movement | Holds / reaction | Continuity & AI prompt / handoff |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **01 · 0–5s** | Establish the moonlit garden. Both adults are separated on a visible path, facing generally toward one another. No approach yet. | Proposed slow forward drift; keep both figures and the path legible. | Brief establishing hold before the cut. | Set the garden layout, moonlit palette, and screen directions. **Prompt:** “Two adult characters stand apart on a winding path in an enchanted moonlit garden; silver-blue light, subtle drifting fireflies, both figures visible, restrained romantic-fantasy mood. Hold their positions.” |
| **02 · 5–12s** | They begin walking toward one another. Keep their paths and relative positions clear; end before they meet. | Proposed lateral tracking move that maintains both in frame; actor motion and camera motion are separate channels. | Let the approach read; no contact or eye-contact claim until visible. | Preserve wardrobe, approach directions, and garden landmarks from Shot 01. **Prompt:** “The same two adults walk toward each other along the same garden path, measured and attentive; maintain their screen directions and spacing, both readable in frame. End while they are still approaching.” |
| **03 · 12–18s** | The designated character slows, stops, and settles. The other continues only as needed to reach the proposed final spacing, then stops. | Proposed tracking move decelerates and settles with the action; avoid an unsupported precise camera path. | Hold after both are settled; make the stopping character’s pause readable. | Define which character stops first before generation. Keep final positions and eyelines consistent with Shot 04. **Prompt:** “The first adult slows to a stop and settles; the second completes the approach and stops opposite them. Keep both in view and preserve the established screen directions. End with both still.” |
| **04 · 18–23s** | Both meet each other’s gaze. Keep the moment simple; no unplanned touch. | Proposed restrained push-in, or use a locked frame if the tool cannot reliably control movement. | Hold the mutual look long enough to register before cutting. | Match the settled positions and eyelines from Shot 03. **Prompt:** “The two adults stand at their established positions and make eye contact. A quiet, vulnerable pause; no new movement or contact. Preserve faces, clothing, lighting, and screen direction.” |
| **05 · 23–27s** | Character A reacts first: a small visible change in expression or posture. Character B remains attentive. | Proposed close framing; cut rather than rely on an unsupported camera transition. | Give A’s reaction room to read. | Keep the eyeline and the same side of the interaction. **Prompt:** “Close view of the established adult character reacting to the shared look with a subtle, readable change in expression; gaze remains toward the other character off-screen. No dialogue or new action.” |
| **06 · 27–30s** | Character B reacts in return; end on a held, emotionally open look. | Proposed reverse close framing; hold steady. | Final reaction hold through the ending. | Match Shot 05’s eyeline, lighting, and screen direction. **Prompt:** “Reverse close view of the other established adult character returning the look with a subtle reaction. Match the prior shot’s eyeline and moonlit lighting; hold the expression to the end.” |

### Continuity and execution notes

- Lock character identities, wardrobe, garden layout, screen directions, and which character stops first before generation. Use approved reference assets if available; a seed alone does not guarantee consistency.
- Treat each row as a separate generation proposal. Confirm the chosen tool’s supported reference, duration, aspect-ratio, and camera controls before writing executable prompts. If camera control is unconfirmed, keep movement as a design intention or use locked-shot alternatives.
- For the stop, verify visible deceleration, planted support, and settling only if the feet and body are actually readable; otherwise record foot contact as unverified.
- Review generated clips for action clarity, matching positions and eyelines, and end-state continuity. Revise one variable at a time. These prompts and timings are a plan, not generated footage or a verified edit.
- **Uncertainty:** final framing, clip durations and handles, tool controls, character designs, aspect ratio, audio, and exact timing need confirmation. No audio is specified or assumed.

## 30-second romantic-fantasy drama — **DESIGN PROPOSAL**

No reference footage was provided, so nothing below is an observation. All timing, blocking, camera moves, and prompt language are proposed for a new production. Times are final-timeline seconds; shot-local time starts at each shot’s in-point. **Proposal only—not a measured edit or confirmed control set for any AI tool.**

**Working assumptions:** two adult characters; moonlit hall; no dialogue specified. Keep one screen direction for the entrant and preserve the existing character’s eyeline across the reveal and reaction.

| Shot / final time | Actor blocking and action phases | Camera / reveal | Hold or reaction | Cut continuity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SH01 · 0–6s** | Character A is already in the hall, still and looking toward the empty entrance. From 4–6s, A registers a sound or presence offscreen with a small head/eye turn. | Wide establishes A, hall, and entrance. **Proposed:** slow push toward A; keep the entrance readable but unoccupied. | Brief hold on the empty entrance before A reacts; let the reaction read before cutting. | Cut on A’s eyeline toward frame right. |
| **SH02 · 6–12s** | Character B enters from offscreen right, crosses the threshold, then pauses. A remains in the background if composition allows. | **Proposed:** medium-wide framing; gentle track or pan to include B. Reveal B at the threshold, not before. | Hold after B stops; allow the pause to land. | B remains screen-right of A; cut with B settled and A’s eyeline directed toward B. |
| **SH03 · 12–18s** | A turns toward B; B holds position. A’s expression shifts from alertness to recognition. | **Proposed:** medium close-up on A; restrained push-in or locked frame. No move required if the reaction reads clearly. | Hold through the recognition; do not cut before the change is legible. | Match A’s eyeline toward frame right into the next shot. |
| **SH04 · 18–24s** | B meets A’s look, then takes one deliberate step into the hall and stops. A stays in place. | **Proposed:** medium on B, with A’s presence or eyeline maintained where feasible. Small track only if needed to keep B framed. | Hold on B’s response after the stop. | Preserve A-left/B-right screen relationship; cut after B settles. |
| **SH05 · 24–30s** | A and B share a quiet look. Optional proposal: A takes a small step toward B; B does not advance. End before contact. | **Proposed:** two-shot; slow, subtle push-in, then settle. | Hold the shared look through the end; avoid implying touch or a further event. | End on a stable shared composition. |

### AI prompt handoff — proposed shot instructions

Use approved character and location references if available; none were supplied. Confirm each generation tool’s reference, duration, aspect-ratio, and camera-control support before treating these as executable controls.

| Shot | Prompt handoff |
|---|---|
| **SH01** | Moonlit hall; adult A already inside, facing an empty entrance. A small turn toward an offscreen presence is the single main action. **Camera proposal:** wide establishing frame with a restrained push-in, ending with A’s attention directed frame right. Preserve clothing, position, and lighting through the shot. |
| **SH02** | Same hall and lighting; adult B enters from offscreen right, crosses the threshold, and stops. A remains oriented toward B. **Camera proposal:** medium-wide framing that reveals B at the threshold. Preserve screen direction and the established hall layout. |
| **SH03** | Adult A turns toward B and shifts from alertness to recognition. **Camera proposal:** medium close-up, locked or with a restrained push-in. End on a readable reaction; preserve A’s frame-right eyeline. |
| **SH04** | Adult B returns A’s look, takes one deliberate step into the hall, and stops. **Camera proposal:** medium framing; move only if needed to retain the composition. End settled, with B still screen-right of A. |
| **SH05** | A and B hold a quiet shared look; optional small step by A, no contact. **Camera proposal:** two-shot with a subtle push-in that settles before the end. Keep both characters readable and preserve their established positions. |

**Uncertainty / checks:** Character designs, wardrobe, hall layout, exact moonlight source, aspect ratio, frame rate, audio, and AI-tool capabilities are unspecified. Confirm those before generation. ## 30-second plan — **DESIGN_PROPOSAL / not an execution-ready board**

Romantic-fantasy mood: intimate and restrained. **All timings, blocking, dialogue, and camera moves below are proposed**, not measured from a reference. Times are final-timeline seconds; shot labels are provisional role names, not registered project IDs. The destination AI tool’s camera, reference, duration, and audio controls are **unverified**.

| Proposed shot | Final time | Blocking and action phases | Camera proposal | Gait/contact visibility, hold, and cut continuity |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| **A — Garden walk** | 0–8s | Two adults walk side by side along a moonlit garden path, sharing a quiet glance. Ease from walking into a stop near the end; one turns slightly toward the other. | Begin in a readable two-shot; gently track with them, then settle as they stop. | Keep both characters’ feet in frame during the approach if feasible; show weight transfer only where clearly visible. Do not imply confirmed foot plants if obscured. Hold their settled eyeline briefly. Cut out on that look. |
| **B — Invitation** | 8–14s | Continue the eyeline in a two-shot. One character says, **“I thought the garden was only a story.”** The other answers, **“Tonight, it’s ours.”** | Mostly locked framing; avoid adding movement without a story reason. | Start on the matching settled look from A. Allow dialogue and a short reaction beat; cut after the reply, preserving screen direction and eyeline. Dialogue is proposed; recording and audio generation are not included. |
| **C — Listening reaction** | 14–22s | Close on the listener. They absorb the reply, then soften into a small smile and glance toward the garden lights. | Gentle push-in is a proposal; keep it subtle and let the expression motivate attention. | No gait. Hold long enough to read the expression change. Cut on the glance toward the lights, not midway through an unclear expression. |
| **D — Shared response** | 22–30s | Return to both characters. They share a look, then turn their attention toward the moonlit garden; end on a quiet shared pause. | Return to a calm two-shot; settle and hold. | Match C’s glance direction. No new walk is required. Preserve the final eyeline and spacing through the end. |

### AI prompt handoff — proposed shot briefs

Use the same approved character and look references across shots if available; no reference assets were supplied. Keep prompts focused on one main action per shot.

- **A:** Two adult characters walk together on a moonlit garden path, sharing a quiet glance. They slow and stop facing one another. Proposed camera: gentle tracking move that settles into a two-shot. Keep wardrobe, spacing, path direction, and lighting consistent. **Foot contact must be checked in the generated result; visibility may be limited.**
- **B:** Same adults, same positions and eyelines, in a calm two-shot. They exchange the proposed short dialogue. Proposed camera: mostly static. Preserve screen direction and facial continuity. **Speech/audio support unverified.**
- **C:** Close reaction of the listener after the reply: thoughtfulness softens into a small smile; their gaze turns toward the garden lights. Proposed gentle push-in. Keep the emotional change readable; do not add dialogue.
- **D:** Return to the same pair and garden layout. They share a look, then face the lights together and hold. Proposed static two-shot; preserve C’s glance direction and both characters’ positions.

### Uncertainty and checks

- No reference video, character designs, location assets, dialogue recording, or tool capability details were supplied.
- Confirm the chosen generator supports the needed clip lengths, references, camera direction, and any requested audio before treating these briefs as executable prompts. Do not assume exact camera values or controls.
- Review generated clips for foot visibility/contact where claimed, consistent character appearance, eyelines, screen direction, dialogue readability, and cut matching. Actual cut timing and reaction holds may need adjustment after viewing.
